title: A study to find out if the study drug elecoglipron helps adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus by comparing it with semaglutide, a medicine already used to treat type 2 diabetes mellitus
official: A Randomized, Open-label, Parallel-group Phase III Study to Evaluate the Efficacy, Safety, and Tolerability of Elecoglipron Compared with Oral Semaglutide in Adults with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (Eluminate-2)
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the efficacy of elecoglipron compared with oral semaglutide for glycemic control
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Diagnosed with T2DM for at least 90 days prior to screening
2. T2DM inadequately managed with lifestyle management alone or up to 2 oral glucose-lowering medications
3. HbA1c value of ≥ 7% to ≤ 10.5% (53 to 91.3 mmol/mol)
4. Increased risk of CV events defined by ≥1 of: documented coronary heart disease, peripheral arterial disease, ischemic cerebrovascular disease, or heart failure (NYHA II–III); or ≥2 CV risk factors
5. BMI of ≥ 23 kg/m2 at screening
6. Stable body weight (self-reported or documented) for 90 days prior to screening
Exclusion criteria:
1. T1DM, secondary forms of diabetes (including congenital forms), or history of ketoacidosis or hyperosmolar coma
2. Currently receiving or anticipated to receive, therapeutic intervention for diabetic retinopathy and/or macular edema
3. Have had more than one episode of severe hypoglycemia within 180 days prior to screening or has a history of hypoglycemia unawareness or poor recognition of hypoglycemic symptoms
4. Clinically significant condition affecting the upper GI tract or chronic use of any medication that affects gastric motility or gastric emptying
5. History of acute or chronic pancreatitis
6. Severe congestive heart failure (NYHA IV)
7. History/family history of medullary thyroid cancer or multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2
